Build a file upload zone in vanilla JS: a drop area (drag-over highlights it), file input fallback, a file list with name/size, image previews, and simulated upload progress bars with cancel. Restrict to images (or accept filter).

Requirements

  • Click-to-browse opens the file picker
  • Drag-over highlights the drop zone
  • Drop adds files to the list (no duplicates)
  • Image previews rendered via URL.createObjectURL
  • Each file shows name, size, and a progress bar
  • Simulated upload with progress + cancel
  • Invalid type shows an error toast

Concepts: dragenter/dragover/drop · URL.createObjectURL · progress simulation · file validation
lessons.why:
• Prevent default on dragover/drop or the browser navigates away. Track a drag counter to avoid flicker on child enter/leave.
  • Progress: setInterval advancing 0->100 per file, or a slow-approach curve (p += (100-p)*0.1). Cancel = clearInterval + mark file failed.

lessons.name: Drag & Drop Reorder / Kanban
lessons.desc: HTML5 DnD with live reordering — the interview favorite that catches everyone.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Drag & Drop Reorder / Kanban
lessons.what:
Build a drag-and-drop list (or single-column kanban) in vanilla JS: drag items to reorder them, with a live insertion indicator (ghost) showing where the item will land. Support dragstart/dragover/drop; the list re-renders from state after every drop.

Requirements

  • Drag an item to reorder it within the list
  • Live visual insertion point while dragging
  • Drop commits the new order (state updates)
  • Only the dragged item moves (not a copy)
  • Drag handle or full-row draggable
  • Keyboard alternative for reordering (bonus)
  • Works with mouse only (touch is bonus)

Concepts: dragstart/dragover/drop · dragenter index math · state-based re-render · visual feedback
lessons.why:
• On dragover, compute the target index from the list items' bounding boxes and show a ghost line before/after that item.
  • On drop: splice the dragged item out of state and back in at the ghost index, then re-render the list. The source item keeps class dragging during the drag.

lessons.name: Toast Notification System
lessons.desc: A queue + auto-dismiss + stacking — the tiny system that separates widget coders.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Toast Notification System
lessons.what:
Build a toast notification system in vanilla JS: a toast(message, type) API (success/info/error/warning), toasts stack in the top-right, auto-dismiss after 4s with a manual close button, and multiple toasts don't overlap. Cap the visible stack (e.g. max 5).

Requirements

  • toast(message, type) exposes the public API
  • Four types with distinct colors/icons
  • Auto-dismiss after 4s with countdown (bonus)
  • Manual close button
  • Toasts stack cleanly (top-right container)
  • Max 5 visible; oldest is removed beyond that
  • A11y: role="status"/"alert" for each toast

Concepts: event emitter / pub-sub · DOM creation · timers · container pattern
lessons.why:
• Create one container div on init (fixed, top-right). Each toast is a div appended with a class per type.
  • Auto-dismiss: setTimeout(remove, 4000). For max N, when length > 5 remove the first child. Close button removes + clears its timer.

lessons.name: Chips / Tags Input
lessons.desc: Enter to add, Backspace to remove, dedupe, and backspace-on-empty — micro-interaction mastery.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Chips / Tags Input
lessons.what:
Build a chips (tags) input in vanilla JS: type a tag, press Enter (or comma) to add it as a chip; chips have an × to remove; pressing Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip; duplicates are rejected with a shake/error. Provide a value getter for the chips.

Requirements

  • Enter or comma commits the typed value as a chip
  • Chips render with a remove (×) button
  • Backspace on empty input removes the last chip
  • Duplicate values rejected with an error flash
  • Leading/trailing whitespace trimmed
  • Input cleared after committing a chip
  • Chips accessible: getChips() returns the array

Concepts: keydown handling · deduplication · chip removal · input width auto-grow
lessons.why:
• Handle keydown on the input: Enter/comma -> commit; Backspace with value=="" -> remove last chip; Escape -> clear.
  • Auto-grow the input: set its width to scrollWidth (or a hidden span mirror) so the text never overflows the pill row.

lessons.name: Snake on Canvas
lessons.desc: Game loop, collision detection, and input buffering on <canvas> — a classic hard round.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Snake on Canvas
lessons.what:
Build Snake on a <canvas> with vanilla JS: a grid-based snake that moves on a fixed tick, grows when it eats food, wraps or dies on walls (your choice — call it out), dies on self-collision, and a score/restart. Arrow/WASD input with direction buffering so a fast turn isn't lost.

Requirements

  • Snake moves on a fixed interval (grid tick)
  • Arrow keys + WASD control direction
  • Direction can't reverse into itself
  • Input buffering: two rapid turns in one tick both register
  • Food spawns randomly on empty cells
  • Eating grows the snake and increments score
  • Self-collision ends the game; restart button
  • Rendered on canvas with clear frame loop

Concepts: game loop · linked-list / queue body model · input buffering · canvas rendering
lessons.why:
• Model the snake as a queue (head at front). Move = unshift(newHead), pop tail (unless growing). Body rendering = draw each cell rect.
  • Input buffer: push direction changes to an array; on each tick shift one and apply only if not the reverse of the current direction.

lessons.name: Minesweeper (flood fill)
lessons.desc: Flood-fill reveal, adjacency counting, and chording — the Google hard favorite.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Minesweeper (flood fill)
lessons.what:
Build Minesweeper in vanilla JS: a 9x9 board with 10 mines, first-click-safe, reveal cells with an adjacent-mine count, flood-fill open zero cells (BFS/DFS), right-click to flag, a win condition (all non-mine cells revealed) and a loss on mine click. Timer + reset.

Requirements

  • 9x9 grid, 10 mines placed randomly
  • First click never hits a mine (move it)
  • Revealing a 0 opens its whole region (flood fill)
  • Numbers show adjacent mine counts
  • Right-click flags/unflags a cell (counter shown)
  • Clicking a mine reveals all and ends the game
  • Win detected when every non-mine cell is revealed
  • Reset reshuffles and restarts

Concepts: flood fill (BFS) · adjacency counting · game state · right-click handling
lessons.why:
• Model as a 2D array of cell objects {mine, revealed, flagged, adj}. BFS stack: push neighbors of revealed 0-cells within bounds, skipping visited.
  • Place mines after the first click using a candidate list excluding the clicked cell + its neighbors. adjacency = count mines among the 8 neighbors.

lessons.name: 2048 Game
lessons.desc: Tile merging, sliding, and spawn logic — the ultimate grid state-machine round.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? 2048 Game
lessons.what:
Build the 2048 game in vanilla JS: a 4x4 grid, arrow keys slide all tiles in that direction, equal adjacent tiles merge (each tile merges once per move), a random 2/4 spawns after each valid move, score tracks merged values, and the game ends when no moves remain (or 2048 is reached).

Requirements

  • Arrow keys slide + merge all tiles
  • A tile merges at most once per move
  • Random 2 (90%) or 4 (10%) spawns after a valid move
  • No-move-on-this-direction leaves the board unchanged
  • Score increments by merged values
  • Win banner at 2048 (continue optional)
  • Game-over detection: board full and no merges possible
  • Animated slide/merge feel (CSS transitions)

Concepts: grid transformation · merge logic · spawn logic · valid-move detection
lessons.why:
• Slide-left algorithm: per row, compress (remove zeros), merge adjacent equals once, re-compress. Rotate the board 4 times to reuse it for all directions.
  • Valid move = any cell changed. Copy board before the attempt (JSON/structured clone) to compare. Possible move check: any empty cell OR any adjacent equal pair.

lessons.name: Drawing Board with Undo/Redo
lessons.desc: Pointer events, stroke recording, and undo/redo snapshots — real product UX.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Drawing Board with Undo/Redo
lessons.what:
Build a drawing board on canvas: draw freehand with the mouse or pen (pointer events), pick color and stroke width, undo/redo stroke-by-stroke, and clear. Snapshots are stored as stroke arrays (not pixel images) so undo is cheap and lossless.

Requirements

  • Freehand drawing via pointer events (down/move/up)
  • Color and stroke-width pickers apply live
  • Undo removes the last stroke; redo restores it
  • Clear wipes the board
  • Stroke model: [{points, color, width}]
  • High-DPI aware: canvas sized to devicePixelRatio
  • Touch support (pointer events unify mouse + touch)

Concepts: Pointer Events · stroke vectorization · undo/redo stacks · canvas DPI scaling
lessons.why:
• pointerdown starts a stroke, pointermove appends points, pointerup closes it and pushes to strokes[]. Redraw = clear + replay every stroke on each change.
  • Undo = strokes.pop() into redo stack; redo pushes back. Because strokes are data, redraw is deterministic.

lessons.name: Virtual Scrolling List
lessons.desc: Render 100,000 rows as ~10 DOM nodes — the performance round everyone flubs.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Virtual Scrolling List
lessons.what:
Build a virtual scrolling list in vanilla JS: render only the visible window of a large array (e.g. 100,000 rows) inside a fixed-height scroll container. On scroll, compute the visible range, render only those rows with absolute/translateY positioning, and keep a small buffer. Variable row heights optional (bonus).

Requirements

  • Fixed-height scroll container
  • Renders only visible rows + buffer (e.g. 5 each side)
  • Row positions via translateY, not top (no layout thrash)
  • Handles 100k+ rows without lag
  • Scroll position stable when jumping to a row
  • Click on a row fires a callback with the row index
  • Resize/row-height change re-measures

Concepts: virtualization · scroll events + rAF throttling · translateY positioning · window/range math
lessons.why:
• scrollTop / rowHeight = firstIndex; visible count = containerHeight / rowHeight; clamp. Render slice [first-buffer, last+buffer] into a spacer div of totalHeight.
  • Use a container div with height = total rows * rowHeight, and absolutely position each row with transform: translateY(index * rowHeight). Throttle scroll with requestAnimationFrame.

lessons.name: Sortable / Filterable Data Table
lessons.desc: Sorting, filtering, and row selection — the most common dashboard component.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Sortable / Filterable Data Table
lessons.what:
Build a data table in vanilla JS from a JSON dataset (name, email, role, status, join date): click a column header to sort asc/desc with an indicator, a search box filters across columns, a status filter chips, and selectable rows with a bulk actions bar. No framework.

Requirements

  • Renders rows from a JSON array
  • Column-header click toggles sort (asc/desc + indicator)
  • Search filters by any column (case-insensitive)
  • Status filter (chips or select)
  • Row selection with checkboxes + bulk delete
  • Empty state when filters match nothing
  • Sorting and filtering compose together

Concepts: sorting comparators · filter predicates · table rendering · state composition
lessons.why:
• Keep state = {sortKey, sortDir, query, status, selected:Set}. Derive rows = useMemo-equivalent: filter then sort then render — compute a fresh array each render.
  • Header click: same key toggles dir, new key sets asc. Icons: ▲/▼. Select all checkbox handles header toggling.

lessons.name: WebSocket Chat UI (vanilla)
lessons.desc: A WebSocket client, message list, and reconnect logic — real-time from the raw API.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? WebSocket Chat UI (vanilla)
lessons.what:
Build a chat UI in vanilla JS talking to a WebSocket endpoint: send messages, render incoming messages (own vs other with different alignment), show typing indicator and online status, auto-scroll to the latest, and reconnect with backoff on disconnect. Include a message input with Enter to send.

Requirements

  • Connects to a WebSocket (ws:// or a mock)
  • Send message via input + Enter/button
  • Renders own vs peer messages with alignment
  • Auto-scrolls to newest unless user scrolled up
  • Online/disconnected status indicator
  • Reconnect with exponential backoff
  • Typing indicator (bonus)
  • Handles connection error gracefully

Concepts: WebSocket API · reconnect backoff · message rendering · scroll anchoring
lessons.why:
• Socket events: onopen/onmessage/onclose/onerror. Track connection state in a status banner. Reconnect: schedule ws = new WebSocket(url) with increasing delay, reset on open.
  • Scroll anchoring: if user is near the bottom (scrollTop near max) auto-scroll after append; otherwise show a "new message" jump chip.

lessons.name: Mini Reactive DOM Framework
lessons.desc: Reactive state -> DOM updates — the tiny framework behind Vue/Solid, built by hand.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Mini Reactive DOM Framework
lessons.what:
Build a minimal reactive framework in vanilla JS: a reactive(state) proxy, watchEffect(fn) that re-runs when its tracked dependencies change, and a bind helper that maps state to DOM nodes (text and attributes). Counter + conditional-render examples prove it works.

Requirements

  • reactive(obj): Proxy tracks reads and writes
  • watchEffect(fn): runs immediately, re-runs on dependency change
  • Dependency tracking: only props read inside fn trigger it
  • bindText(el, state, path): keeps el.textContent in sync
  • bindAttr(el, attr, state, path): attribute binding
  • Multiple effects on one property all fire
  • Nested state objects are also reactive

Concepts: Proxy · dependency tracking · effect scheduling · WeakMap
lessons.why:
• Track: global activeEffect; Proxy get registers (target, key) -> activeEffect in a WeakMap>>. Trigger: Proxy set runs those effects.
  • watchEffect: set activeEffect = fn, run fn(), clear. Batch with a microtask queue (Promise.then) so multiple writes in one tick run effects once.

lessons.name: Virtual DOM Diff (vanilla)
lessons.desc: createElement, mount, and patch — build the React reconciliation core in vanilla.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Virtual DOM Diff (vanilla)
lessons.what:
Implement a minimal virtual DOM in vanilla JS: h(type, props, ...children) creates vnodes, mount(vnode, container) builds real DOM, and patch(oldVnode, newVnode, parent) diffs and updates in place. Props diff by key; children diff by index; text nodes optimized.

Requirements

  • h(): vnode = {type, props, children} (text as strings)
  • mount(): creates real nodes from vnodes
  • patch(): same type -> diff props + children
  • patch(): different type -> replace subtree
  • Prop diff: set/remove only changed attributes
  • Children diff by index with reuse
  • Event props (onclick) attach as listeners
  • Keys for list children (bonus)

Concepts: recursion · diffing · event delegation · object comparison
lessons.why:
• patch props: iterate new keys -> setAttribute / addEventListener (skip if equal to old), iterate old keys missing in new -> removeAttribute. Compare with Object.is to skip.
  • patch children: walk both arrays together, patch pairs, append extras, remove leftovers. Text: if both strings and different -> node.textContent = newText.

lessons.name: Spreadsheet Grid with Formulas
lessons.desc: A grid of cells, formula evaluation, and dependency recalculation — the wildcard round.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Spreadsheet Grid with Formulas
lessons.what:
Build a spreadsheet in vanilla JS: a 10x10 editable grid (A1, B1, ...), clicking a cell edits it inline, cells support raw values and formulas like =A1+B2, =SUM(A1:A5), =AVG(B1:B10). Evaluate formulas with dependency tracking so editing A1 recalculates every cell that references it (topological order).

Requirements

  • Renders an editable NxM grid with column/row labels
  • Inline cell editing (Enter commits, Escape cancels)
  • Values persist in a state object keyed by cell id
  • Formulas start with = and parse references + SUM/AVG
  • Cells referencing other cells recalculate on change
  • Circular reference detection (error state)
  • Display vs raw value: formula shows its result

Concepts: formula parsing · dependency graph · topological ordering · grid rendering
lessons.why:
• Parse references with a regex for ([A-J])(d+). Build a dependency graph cell -> dependents. On edit, recompute affected cells in topological order.
  • Eval safely: build the expression by substituting referenced cell values, then evaluate with new Function(...)? Safer: write a tiny recursive-descent evaluator handling + - * / and SUM/AVG over ranges.

lessons.name: File Explorer (Folder Tree)
lessons.desc: A recursive folder tree with expand/collapse, CRUD, and rename — recursion in the DOM.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? File Explorer (Folder Tree)
lessons.what:
Build a file explorer in vanilla JS from a nested {name, type: 'folder'|'file', children?} tree: render the hierarchy recursively, folders expand/collapse with an arrow, files select on click, and the toolbar supports new folder / new file / rename / delete on the selected node. Empty folders, deep nesting, and indentation guides.

Requirements

  • Renders the full tree recursively (folder > file nesting)
  • Folder arrow toggles expand/collapse; state persists
  • Click selects a node (highlight + toolbar enabled)
  • New folder / new file creates a child under the selected folder
  • Rename edits the node name inline (Enter/Escape)
  • Delete removes the node and its whole subtree
  • Folder name length/path-depth edge cases handled
  • Indentation guides render for each depth level

Concepts: recursive rendering · tree CRUD · immutable tree updates · event delegation
lessons.why:
• Model state as a single tree object; all operations return a new tree (map over children recursively). Render one recursive function renderNode(node, depth) and compose containers.
  • Delegation: one click listener reads data-id, resolves the node path, then rerenders. Paths: keep a path array (indices) in data-path so operations can rebuild the tree immutably.

lessons.name: Nested Comments (Reddit-style)
lessons.desc: Recursive comment threads with reply, delete, and vote — the infinite-nesting classic.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Nested Comments (Reddit-style)
lessons.what:
Build nested comments in vanilla JS: a top-level comment box, replies nest recursively to any depth, each comment has reply / upvote-downvote / delete (with a confirm). Reply opens an inline editor, and every comment shows an author, relative time, and score. A collapse toggle hides a comment and all of its children.

Requirements

  • Comments render as a recursive thread tree
  • Reply adds a child comment to any depth
  • Inline reply editor (textarea + post/cancel)
  • Upvote/downvote increments a score (one vote per comment)
  • Delete removes the comment and all descendants
  • Collapse toggle hides a comment and its subtree
  • Authors + relative timestamps rendered
  • No framework: pure DOM building + event delegation

Concepts: recursive rendering · tree state updates · event delegation · voting state
lessons.why:
• Comment node = {id, author, text, time, score, children[]}. renderThread(comment) returns the DOM for that subtree; rerender the whole thread on every mutation (data is small).
  • Reply: keep editingCommentId in state; the editor renders inline under that node. Deleting = filter node out recursively via map over children.

lessons.name: JSON Tree Viewer
lessons.desc: Render any JSON as a collapsible, color-coded tree — recursion over mixed data.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? JSON Tree Viewer
lessons.what:
Build a JSON tree viewer in vanilla JS: paste any JSON (or load a sample) and render it as an indented, collapsible tree — objects and arrays expand/collapse with a toggle, primitives are color-coded (string green, number blue, boolean purple, null gray), keys are clickable to copy the path, and a search box highlights + jumps to matching keys.

Requirements

  • Parses JSON input (error state for invalid)
  • Objects and arrays render with expand/collapse toggles
  • Type-based color coding for primitives
  • Keys copy their JSONPath on click (e.g. a.b[0].c)
  • Search highlights matching keys and jumps to first
  • Large inputs stay responsive (lazy render children)
  • Empty object/array shown inline as {} / []

Concepts: recursive rendering · mixed-type introspection · JSONPath · lazy expansion
lessons.why:
• One recursive renderValue(key, value, path) returns a node. If value is an object/array, it creates a togglable branch that lazily renders children only when expanded.
  • Path: build by concatenation (array adds [i], object adds .key). For search, precompute a flat index of key paths once, then highlight/scroll on match.

lessons.name: Cascading Checkbox Tree
lessons.desc: Parent-child checked-state propagation with indeterminate boxes — recursive state math.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Cascading Checkbox Tree
lessons.what:
Build a cascading checkbox tree in vanilla JS from a nested permissions list (e.g. Settings > Notifications > Email): checking a parent checks all descendants, unchecking clears all, a partially-checked parent renders an indeterminate box, and any manual child change recomputes ancestors. A footer shows the total selected / total count.

Requirements

  • Renders a nested checkbox list recursively
  • Checking a parent checks its entire subtree
  • Unchecking a parent unchecks its entire subtree
  • Parent with some checked children shows indeterminate state
  • Manual child toggle recomputes all ancestors
  • Leaf count + selected count shown in the footer
  • Checkbox + label click both toggle the node

Concepts: recursive state propagation · indeterminate state · derived state · tree traversal
lessons.why:
• Derive, don't store: a node's state is computed from its children — all checked, none, or mixed. Store only leaf 'checked' booleans (or a Set of checked ids) and compute everything else.
  • A checkbox indeterminate property: set el.indeterminate (not a CSS class). After any change, walk up recomputing each ancestor from its children.

lessons.name: Directory Size Calculator
lessons.desc: Recursive size aggregation over a fake filesystem — the math behind disk-usage tools.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Directory Size Calculator
lessons.what:
Build a directory size calculator in vanilla JS: a fake file tree where files carry byte sizes and folders aggregate their subtree total, rendered with each node's size right-aligned. Expand/collapse folders, sort children by size desc, and a 'calculate all' scan that animates folder totals filling in (walking the tree recursively with a delay).

Requirements

  • File tree with per-file sizes and folders aggregating subtrees
  • Size shown right-aligned per row, formatted (B/KB/MB)
  • Expand/collapse folders
  • Sort children by size descending (toggle)
  • Scan animation: folder totals fill in bottom-up
  • Recursive aggregation computes totals once and caches
  • Large trees: total displayed at the root

Concepts: recursive aggregation · post-order traversal · size formatting · animation timing
lessons.why:
• A folder's size = sum of children, computed post-order: size(node) = files sum + folders.map(size). Cache results in a Map so toggling sort doesn't recompute.
  • For the scan animation, flatten the post-order sequence into a list, then reveal each folder's total on a setTimeout/setInterval tick (or rAF).

lessons.name: Todo App with Filters
lessons.desc: The "Hello World" of machine coding. But nailing the edge cases sets you apart.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Todo App with Filters
lessons.what:
Build a Todo App with: add, delete, toggle complete. Filter by All/Active/Completed. Show count of active items. Persist to localStorage. Support editing a todo inline on double-click.

Requirements

  • Add todo on Enter key or button click
  • Toggle individual todo complete/incomplete
  • Delete individual todo
  • Filter: All / Active / Completed tabs
  • Show "X items left" count
  • Persist todos to localStorage
  • Inline edit on double-click (blur or Enter to save)

Concepts: useState · useEffect · array methods · localStorage · controlled inputs
lessons.why:
• Use a todos array in state: [{id, text, completed}]. Filter is separate state. Derive filtered list at render time, not in state.
  • For inline editing: store an editingId state. Double-click sets it. Render an instead of for that item.

lessons.name: Accordion Component
lessons.desc: Test component API design and state management — are you making it configurable?
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Accordion Component
lessons.what:
Build an Accordion component. Accept items as [{id, title, content}]. Support two modes: single (only one panel open at a time) and multiple (many can be open). Add smooth CSS transition. Support keyboard navigation.

Requirements

  • Single mode: opening one closes others
  • Multiple mode: independent toggles
  • Smooth height transition on open/close
  • Keyboard: Enter/Space to toggle focused item
  • Controlled and uncontrolled modes (defaultOpen prop vs open prop)
  • ARIA attributes (aria-expanded, aria-controls)

Concepts: useState · props · controlled vs uncontrolled · ARIA · CSS transitions
lessons.why:
• Single mode: store openId (one value). Multiple mode: store Set of openIds. Render conditionally based on whether item.id is in the open set.
  • For smooth height: use max-height transition from 0 to max-content. Or use a ref to measure content height and animate to it.

lessons.name: Modal / Dialog Component
lessons.desc: Looks simple. The gotchas (focus trap, scroll lock, portal) reveal your seniority.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Modal / Dialog Component
lessons.what:
Build a reusable Modal component. It should: render in a portal, trap focus inside, close on backdrop click and ESC key, lock body scroll when open, and support a header/footer/body layout.

Requirements

  • Render into document.body via createPortal
  • Close on backdrop click (not on modal content click)
  • Close on ESC keydown
  • Lock body scroll (overflow: hidden) while open
  • Focus trap: Tab cycles only inside modal
  • First focusable element receives focus on open
  • Restore focus to trigger element on close

Concepts: useEffect · createPortal · refs · keyboard events · focus management
lessons.why:
• Use useRef to store the element that had focus before modal opened. On close, call storedRef.current.focus().
  • Focus trap: on keydown Tab, check if focused element is the last focusable. If yes, move to first. Query all focusable elements inside the modal.

lessons.name: Star Rating Component
lessons.desc: Simple to describe, tricky to make accessible. A favourite in UI-heavy interviews.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Star Rating Component
lessons.what:
Build a StarRating component with: controlled rating, hover preview, half-star support, readonly mode, and custom size/color. Fire onChange(rating) callback.

Requirements

  • Render N stars (default 5, configurable)
  • Hover over a star previews that rating
  • Click sets the rating (fires onChange)
  • Readonly mode: no interaction
  • Half-star: hovering left half of star = x.5 rating
  • ARIA: role="radiogroup", each star role="radio" with aria-checked

Concepts: useState · mouse events · controlled components · ARIA · CSS
lessons.why:
• Track hoverRating and selectedRating separately. Display = hoverRating ?? selectedRating. Reset hoverRating on mouse leave.
  • Half-star: attach onClick to left and right halves of each star div. Calculate half positions with onMouseMove and getBoundingClientRect.

lessons.name: Tabs Component
lessons.desc: Focus on keyboard navigation and lazy rendering — that's what separates good from great.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Tabs Component
lessons.what:
Build a Tabs component accepting [{id, label, content}]. Support: keyboard navigation (arrow keys), lazy loading panels, controlled and uncontrolled modes, and vertical/horizontal orientation.

Requirements

  • Click tab to show panel
  • Arrow Left/Right (horizontal) or Up/Down (vertical) to navigate
  • Home/End keys jump to first/last tab
  • Lazy: only render panel content when tab has been active (mount once, keep in DOM)
  • ARIA: role="tablist", role="tab", role="tabpanel", aria-selected

Concepts: useState · keyboard events · ARIA · lazy rendering · controlled components
lessons.why:
• For lazy rendering: track a Set of "everActivated" tab ids. Only render panel if id is in the set. Display with visibility/hidden instead of unmounting.
  • For keyboard: keep a ref to all tab elements. On arrow key, focus the adjacent tab using tabRef[newIndex].focus().

lessons.name: Countdown Timer
lessons.desc: Interval management, cleanup, and correct time math — all in one component.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Countdown Timer
lessons.what:
Build a CountdownTimer component. Accept duration in seconds. Show MM:SS display. Start, Pause, Reset controls. Show a circular progress ring. Fire onComplete callback when timer hits zero.

Requirements

  • Start/pause/reset controls work correctly
  • Display MM:SS format
  • Circular SVG progress ring reflects remaining %
  • Fires onComplete callback at zero
  • Pausing and resuming is accurate (no drift)
  • Color changes: green → yellow (50%) → red (10%)

Concepts: useState · useEffect · setInterval cleanup · SVG · useRef
lessons.why:
• Use setInterval inside useEffect. Clear it on pause/unmount. Store remaining time in state. On each tick, decrement and check for zero.
  • For the SVG ring: circumference = 2*π*r. stroke-dashoffset = circumference * (1 - progress). Animate with CSS transition.

lessons.name: Pagination Component
lessons.desc: Ellipsis logic and edge cases are where people get tripped up.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Pagination Component
lessons.what:
Build a Pagination component. Props: totalItems, itemsPerPage, currentPage, onPageChange. Render page numbers with prev/next buttons. Show ellipsis (...) for large page counts. Always show first, last, and ±1 around current page.

Requirements

  • Prev/Next buttons (disabled at boundaries)
  • Page number buttons, click fires onPageChange(page)
  • Ellipsis logic: [1] ... [4,5,6] ... [20] pattern
  • Always show first and last page
  • Jump to first/last page buttons (bonus)
  • No internal state — fully controlled component

Concepts: controlled components · array generation · conditional rendering · Math
lessons.why:
• Calculate visible pages: always include 1 and last. Include currentPage ±1. Fill gaps. Add "..." where consecutive pages are skipped (gap > 1).
  • Build an array of page "tokens" — numbers or "..." strings. Map over them to render buttons or ellipsis spans.

lessons.name: OTP Input Component
lessons.desc: A favourite at product companies — tests DOM ref management and UX edge cases.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? OTP Input Component
lessons.what:
Build an OTPInput component that renders N single-character inputs. Auto-focus next on input. Backspace on empty input focuses previous. Support paste (fill all boxes). Fires onChange(otpString) when all filled.

Requirements

  • Renders N input boxes (configurable, default 6)
  • Auto-focus next input after character is typed
  • Backspace on empty: focus previous input
  • Paste: distribute pasted characters across boxes
  • Only allows numeric input (or configurable: numeric/alphanumeric)
  • Fires onChange when all N boxes are filled

Concepts: useRef · array of refs · keyboard events · paste events · controlled inputs
lessons.why:
• Store an array of refs (one per input). On input: move focus to refs[i+1]. On backspace (key, not input): if empty, move to refs[i-1].
  • Paste: e.clipboardData.getData("text"). Slice into N chars, update all boxes, focus last filled box.

lessons.name: Searchable Dropdown
lessons.desc: Keyboard navigation + controlled filtering + accessibility — a full UI challenge.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Searchable Dropdown
lessons.what:
Build a SearchableDropdown with: text input that filters options, keyboard navigation (Up/Down/Enter/Escape), click outside to close, highlight active option, and a "no results" state.

Requirements

  • Text input filters displayed options in real-time
  • Down/Up arrows move active option index
  • Enter selects active option
  • Escape closes dropdown
  • Click outside closes dropdown
  • Highlight matched text in option labels
  • Empty state: "No options found"

Concepts: useState · useRef · useEffect · keyboard events · outside click detection
lessons.why:
• Use a ref on the container div for outside click detection. useEffect: document.addEventListener("mousedown", handler). Check if ref.current.contains(event.target).
  • For text highlighting: split option label by the search term and wrap matching parts in .

lessons.name: Progress Bar Component
lessons.desc: Clamping, threshold colors, and indeterminate mode - the small details interviewers check.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Progress Bar Component
lessons.what:
Build a ProgressBar component with props value, max (default 100), and color. Clamp value to [0, max]. Support threshold-based color zones and an indeterminate animation mode.

Requirements

  • value clamped between 0 and max (no negative or overflowing width)
  • Width computed as value / max * 100%
  • Threshold zones via a config prop (danger/warning/success colors)
  • Indeterminate mode: continuous animation, no value shown
  • Accessible: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max
  • Optional text label on the left and percentage on the right

Concepts: CSS width transition · Math.min/Math.max clamping · conditional styling · ARIA
lessons.why:
• const pct = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, value / max * 100)). Render a track div and a fill div whose width = pct%.
  • Color: pct < 30 ? danger : pct < 70 ? warning : success. Add a CSS transition on width for the smooth fill animation.

lessons.name: Theme Toggle (Dark/Light)
lessons.desc: The ubiquitous product question - CSS variables, persistence, and system preference.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Theme Toggle (Dark/Light)
lessons.what:
Build a ThemeToggle that switches between light and dark themes. Persist the choice in localStorage. On the first visit, respect prefers-color-scheme. Apply the theme via a data-theme attribute on the root element and CSS custom properties.

Requirements

  • Toggle button switches the theme with a smooth transition
  • Selection persisted to localStorage and restored on reload
  • First visit uses the prefers-color-scheme media query
  • Theme applied via data-theme="dark" attribute + CSS variables
  • No flash of the wrong theme on load (inline early init)
  • aria-pressed reflects the current theme for screen readers

Concepts: CSS variables · localStorage · prefers-color-scheme · useEffect
lessons.why:
• Define CSS vars on :root for light and on [data-theme="dark"] for dark. Theme state = localStorage.theme ?? system preference.
  • For no-flash: set document.documentElement.dataset.theme in a tiny inline script before the app hydrates.

lessons.name: Traffic Light
lessons.desc: A state machine disguised as a UI - every product-company loop interview has a variant.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Traffic Light
lessons.what:
Build a TrafficLight component that cycles Red (3s) -> Green (3s) -> Yellow (1s) automatically. A control panel lets you pause/resume and manually switch colors (manual mode cancels the auto-cycle until resumed).

Requirements

  • Auto cycle: Red 3s -> Green 3s -> Yellow 1s, repeating
  • Only one bulb lit at a time
  • Pause/Resume buttons freeze and continue the cycle
  • Manual color buttons switch immediately and pause the cycle
  • Resume restarts the auto-cycle from the current color
  • Durations configurable via a prop
  • Accessible: role="status" announces the current color

Concepts: useEffect · state machine · setTimeout vs setInterval · cleanup
lessons.why:
• Model state as {color, manual}. One useEffect keyed on color schedules the next transition with setTimeout(duration); clear it on pause or unmount.
  • Manual click: setColor and setManual(true). Resume: setManual(false) so the effect re-runs and continues the cycle.

lessons.name: Grid Light (Flipkart)
lessons.desc: The exact Flipkart machine coding round: click a cell, then watch the chain reaction.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Grid Light (Flipkart)
lessons.what:
Build a GridLight game. Render a 3x3 (configurable N x M) grid of cells. Clicking a cell lights it up. When ALL cells are lit, turn them off one by one in reverse click order, 500ms apart.

Requirements

  • Configurable grid size (rows, cols)
  • Click turns a cell on (one-way: off -> on)
  • Track the order in which cells were lit
  • When all cells are lit, turn them off in reverse click order, 500ms apart
  • Input locked during the reset animation
  • Restart/new-game button clears all state
  • Cells are square buttons with clear lit/unlit visuals

Concepts: useState · setTimeout chain · queue ordering · disable during animation
lessons.why:
• Keep an order[] state. When order.length === total cells, schedule order.forEach((id, i) => setTimeout(() => clearCell(id), i * 500)).
  • Guard clicks with an isResetting ref so users cannot add cells mid-animation.

lessons.name: Responsive Navbar with Mobile Menu
lessons.desc: Navigation is a staple - hamburger menu, scroll behaviour, and active states.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Responsive Navbar with Mobile Menu
lessons.what:
Build a Navbar component. Desktop: horizontal links. Mobile (below 768px): a hamburger icon toggles a dropdown menu. Highlight the active link via scroll-spy. Support click-outside close, ESC close, smooth scrolling, and a sticky navbar with a shadow after scrolling.

Requirements

  • Desktop layout: logo + horizontal nav links
  • Mobile: hamburger button opens/closes the menu
  • Menu closes on link click, outside click, and ESC
  • Active link highlighted via IntersectionObserver scroll-spy
  • Sticky navbar with a shadow only after 10px of scroll
  • Accessible: aria-expanded on the hamburger, aria-label on the nav
  • Smooth scrolling to anchors

Concepts: useState · useEffect · useRef · media queries · IntersectionObserver · outside click
lessons.why:
• Track open state plus a ref on the nav wrapper for outside-click detection (document mousedown + contains check).
  • Scroll-spy: observe the sections, set activeId to the section closest to the top of the viewport.

lessons.name: Stepper / Steps Indicator
lessons.desc: The progress tracker MakeMyTrip asked in their SSE round - dynamic step count, one active step.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Stepper / Steps Indicator
lessons.what:
Build a Stepper component that renders a horizontal step indicator: completed steps (check), the active step (highlighted), and upcoming steps, joined by connectors. Support dynamic step count, click-to-navigate, a vertical variant, and onChange(stepIndex).

Requirements

  • Render N steps with connectors between them
  • Per-step states: completed (check), active (current), upcoming
  • Steps configurable via [{label, status?}] or controlled through a current prop
  • Clicking a step navigates to it (fires onChange)
  • Adding/removing steps re-renders correctly
  • Vertical orientation variant
  • Accessible: aria-current="step" on the active step

Concepts: array rendering · controlled vs uncontrolled · conditional styling · ARIA
lessons.why:
• Track currentStep state. status(i) = i < current ? done : i === current ? active : upcoming. Render circles + connectors between them.
  • A connector between steps i and i+1 is filled when i < current.

lessons.name: Autocomplete with Debounce + Highlight
lessons.desc: The canonical React UI machine coding problem. Debounce, API, keyboard nav, highlight.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Autocomplete with Debounce + Highlight
lessons.what:
Build a production-quality Autocomplete component. Debounce the API call (300ms). Keyboard navigate results (Up/Down/Enter/Escape). Highlight matched text. Show loading/error states. Cache results to avoid duplicate requests.

Requirements

  • Debounce API call by 300ms
  • Show loading spinner during fetch
  • Keyboard navigation: Up/Down move selection, Enter picks it, Escape closes
  • Highlight matching substring in each result
  • Cache results by query string (avoid duplicate API calls)
  • Handle API errors gracefully with retry option
  • Clear input button

Concepts: useCallback · useRef · debounce · useReducer for complex state · caching
lessons.why:
• Use useRef for the debounce timer (not state — avoids re-renders). Cache with a useRef Map: queryCache.current.get(query).
  • Manage state with useReducer: {results, loading, error, selectedIndex, isOpen}. Each action updates the right slice.

lessons.name: Infinite Scroll List
lessons.desc: IntersectionObserver + pagination + race conditions — all the real-world complexity.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Infinite Scroll List
lessons.what:
Build an InfiniteScrollList component. Fetch paginated data. Show a loading indicator at the bottom. When the indicator is visible, load the next page. Handle: loading state, error state, end-of-data state, and duplicate fetch prevention.

Requirements

  • Use IntersectionObserver on a sentinel element at the bottom
  • Fetch next page when sentinel enters viewport
  • Show skeleton/spinner while loading next page
  • Show "All items loaded" when data is exhausted
  • Prevent duplicate requests (lock during in-flight fetch)
  • Error boundary + retry button on fetch failure

Concepts: useEffect · useRef · IntersectionObserver · async state · pagination
lessons.why:
• Create a ref on a
    at the bottom of the list. useEffect: observe it. When intersecting and not loading and hasMore, call fetchNextPage().
  • Prevent duplicate: use a loading ref (not state) to check inside the observer callback — state inside closures is stale.

lessons.name: Multi-step Form with Validation
lessons.desc: The most common enterprise machine coding — form state, validation, and navigation.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Multi-step Form with Validation
lessons.what:
Build a MultiStepForm with: 3+ steps (Personal → Professional → Review), per-step validation, a progress indicator, back/forward navigation, form state persistence across steps, and final submit.

Requirements

  • Progress bar shows current step number and %
  • Validate current step before allowing Next
  • Show field-level error messages on submit attempt or blur
  • Back navigation preserves entered data
  • Review step shows all entered data for confirmation
  • Submit button only on last step, shows loading state
  • Disable browser back button from losing form data (warn)

Concepts: useReducer · controlled inputs · validation · multi-step state · useContext
lessons.why:
• Use useReducer with { currentStep, formData, errors }. Action types: NEXT, BACK, SET_FIELD, SET_ERRORS.
  • Validation: run validators per step on NEXT action. If errors, update state.errors and block step change.

lessons.name: Sortable + Filterable Data Table
lessons.desc: Tables are everywhere in B2B products. Performance and UX are both tested here.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Sortable + Filterable Data Table
lessons.what:
Build a DataTable component with: column sorting (asc/desc toggle), global search filter, column-level filters, pagination, column visibility toggle, and row selection (with "select all").

Requirements

  • Sort by clicking column header (asc → desc → none cycle)
  • Global search filters across all string columns
  • Pagination (configurable page size)
  • Column visibility toggles in a dropdown
  • Row checkboxes + "select all" in header
  • Highlight sorted column
  • Show total results count and current range

Concepts: useMemo · sorting/filtering algorithms · controlled vs derived state · performance
lessons.why:
• Derive sortedData and filteredData from raw data using useMemo. Never mutate the original.
  • Sort state: {column: null, direction: "asc"}. On click: toggle direction if same column, else set new column as "asc".

lessons.name: Toast Notification System
lessons.desc: A real utility component — context, portals, animations, auto-dismiss.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Toast Notification System
lessons.what:
Build a Toast system with: global toast() function, 4 types (success/error/warning/info), stack multiple toasts, auto-dismiss with configurable duration, pause on hover, progress bar, manual dismiss, and position (top-right, bottom-left, etc.).

Requirements

  • Global API: toast.success("msg"), toast.error("msg", {duration:5000})
  • Stack up to 5 toasts (oldest auto-removed)
  • Auto-dismiss after duration (default 3s)
  • Pause countdown on hover, resume on mouse leave
  • Animated enter and exit (slide + fade)
  • Manual close button on each toast
  • Rendered in a Portal

Concepts: useContext · createPortal · useReducer · CSS animations · timers
lessons.why:
• Store toasts in a Context. Provide addToast/removeToast. Each toast has id (Date.now()), type, message, duration.
  • For pause on hover: on mouseenter, clear the auto-dismiss timer. Store remaining time. On mouseleave, set a new timer with the remaining time.

lessons.name: Kanban Board with Drag & Drop
lessons.desc: The hardest React beginner-ish problem. Drag & drop + state management is the gauntlet.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Kanban Board with Drag & Drop
lessons.what:
Build a Kanban Board with columns (Todo/In Progress/Done). Drag cards between columns and reorder within columns. Add/delete cards. Persist to localStorage. Without using any drag-and-drop library.

Requirements

  • Drag a card from any column to any other column
  • Reorder cards within a column by dragging
  • Add new card to any column (inline input)
  • Delete card
  • Dragging shows a visual indicator of drop target
  • State persists to localStorage
  • Built using HTML5 Drag and Drop API (no library)

Concepts: useReducer · HTML5 drag API · localStorage · array manipulation · event handling
lessons.why:
• Use HTML5: draggable="true", onDragStart (store cardId+sourceCol in a ref), onDragOver (preventDefault to enable drop), onDrop (move card).
  • State shape: { columns: { todo: [...cards], inprogress: [...], done: [...] } }. Dispatch MOVE_CARD(cardId, fromCol, toCol, targetIndex).

lessons.name: Shopping Cart
lessons.desc: Classic e-commerce feature — tests useReducer, derived state, and UX completeness.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Shopping Cart
lessons.what:
Build a ShoppingCart. Product list with "Add to cart". Cart sidebar/drawer with: quantity controls (+/-/remove), subtotal per item, cart total, tax calculation, discount code field, checkout button.

Requirements

  • Add product to cart (increment if already in cart)
  • Increase/decrease quantity in cart, remove at 0
  • Show subtotal per item, cart total, tax (10%)
  • Apply discount code (SAVE10 = 10% off, SAVE20 = 20%)
  • "Cart is empty" state with CTA
  • Cart item count badge on cart icon
  • Persist cart to localStorage

Concepts: useReducer · derived state · localStorage · conditional rendering
lessons.why:
• Cart state: Map/array of {productId, quantity}. Derive total = cartItems.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.quantity, 0).
  • Discount: store appliedCode in state. Apply multiplier to total at render time.

lessons.name: File Upload with Preview & Progress
lessons.desc: File handling, validation, and simulated progress — a very common product company question.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? File Upload with Preview & Progress
lessons.what:
Build a FileUpload component with: drag-and-drop zone, file validation (type/size), multi-file queue, upload progress per file, cancel individual upload, preview for images.

Requirements

  • Drag-and-drop zone + click to browse
  • File type validation (configurable accepted types)
  • File size validation (max size prop)
  • Show thumbnail preview for image files
  • Per-file progress bar (simulate with setInterval or real XHR)
  • Cancel in-flight upload (AbortController)
  • Retry failed uploads

Concepts: useReducer · File API · drag events · FileReader · AbortController
lessons.why:
• FileReader.readAsDataURL(file) for image previews. Store preview URLs in state.
  • For cancel: store an AbortController per upload. On cancel, call controller.abort(). Clean up in useEffect return.

lessons.name: Image Carousel / Slider
lessons.desc: Microsoft and Google ask this constantly - infinite loop, transitions, and thumbnails.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Image Carousel / Slider
lessons.what:
Build an ImageCarousel component with props images[] and optional autoPlayInterval. Features: next/prev arrows, dot indicators, clickable thumbnails, infinite wrap-around, auto-play with pause on hover, and smooth slide transitions. Handle 1-image and 0-image edge cases.

Requirements

  • Next/Prev buttons cycle images and wrap around infinitely
  • Dot indicators reflect and jump to the active image
  • Auto-play every N seconds; pauses on hover and on manual interaction
  • Smooth slide/translate transition between images
  • Thumbnail strip (configurable)
  • Edge cases: 1 image hides the arrows, 0 images shows an empty state
  • Adjacent images preloaded for fast navigation

Concepts: useState · useRef · setInterval · CSS transform · index modulo
lessons.why:
• Track an index state. next = (index + 1) % len, prev = (index - 1 + len) % len. Render a flex track translated by -index * 100%.
  • Auto-play: setInterval inside a useEffect keyed on paused and index; clear on hover via onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave.

lessons.name: Chips / Tags Input
lessons.desc: Invite chips, tag inputs, email chips - the same problem at every product company.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Chips / Tags Input
lessons.what:
Build a ChipsInput component. Type a value and press Enter or comma to add a chip. Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip; Backspace on a focused chip removes it. Support duplicate prevention, max chips, a validation callback, and a suggestions dropdown. Fire onChange(values).

Requirements

  • Enter or comma adds the typed text as a chip
  • Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip
  • Backspace on a focused chip removes that chip
  • Duplicates and invalid values rejected via a validation callback
  • Optional max chips limit
  • Suggestions dropdown filtered by input; arrows + Enter to pick
  • Chips removable via their x button
  • Controlled: onChange(values) reflects the chips array

Concepts: controlled inputs · keyboard events · array state · focus management
lessons.why:
• values as string[] state. onKeyDown: Enter/comma validates, adds, and clears the input; Backspace when the input is empty pops the last chip.
  • Give each chip a tabIndex. In the Backspace handler, check document.activeElement === chip to remove a focused chip.

lessons.name: Transfer List
lessons.desc: FrontendAtlas staple - bulk moves, disabled actions, and two-pane selection.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Transfer List
lessons.what:
Build a TransferList component with two panes: Available (left) and Selected (right). Check items then move them with bulk action buttons. Disable actions when nothing is selected. Support select-all per pane, independent search, move-all, and item counts.

Requirements

  • Checkboxes per item in both panes
  • Bulk buttons: Move to selected -> and <- Move to available
  • Bulk buttons disabled when the respective pane has no checked items
  • Select-all checkbox per pane (indeterminate when partial)
  • Search box filters each pane independently
  • Move-all quick actions
  • Item counts per pane (3 of 10 selected)

Concepts: Set state · bulk actions · indeterminate checkbox · filtering
lessons.why:
• Keep available[], selected[], and two checked Sets. Transfer = remove from the source list, add to the target, clear its checked set.
  • Select-all checked = checked.size === list.length; indeterminate = checked.size > 0 and < list.length - set the DOM indeterminate property via a ref.

lessons.name: Nested Checkbox Tree
lessons.desc: Parent-child sync with indeterminate states - a FrontendAtlas and GreatFrontend favourite.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Nested Checkbox Tree
lessons.what:
Build a CheckboxTree from nested data: [{id, label, children?}]. Each parent checkbox reflects checked (all children checked), unchecked (none), or indeterminate (some). Checking a parent toggles all descendants; checking a child recomputes ancestors. Support expand/collapse, defaultExpanded, and a search that auto-expands matches.

Requirements

  • Recursive tree rendering with per-node expand/collapse
  • Parent state derived from children: checked / unchecked / indeterminate
  • Toggling a parent toggles all descendants
  • Toggling a leaf recomputes every ancestor state
  • Expand-all / collapse-all buttons
  • Search highlights and auto-expands matching branches
  • onChange(checkedIds) emits the flat set of checked ids

Concepts: recursive components · derived state · indeterminate · tree data structures
lessons.why:
• checkedIds as a Set of ids. Each node derives its state from the set: all children in it -> checked, none -> unchecked, else indeterminate. Set input.checked and input.indeterminate via a ref.
  • Toggling a parent = toggling every descendant id in the set; the children set derives the ancestors automatically on the next render.

lessons.name: Cookie Consent Banner
lessons.desc: The Atlassian browser-round favourite - pure UI flow with localStorage state.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Cookie Consent Banner
lessons.what:
Build a CookieConsent banner that appears at the bottom after a delay. Buttons: Accept All, Reject, and a Settings panel to toggle categories (Essential, Analytics, Marketing). Persist the choice in localStorage so returning users never see it again.

Requirements

  • Banner appears after a configurable delay (default 2s)
  • Accept All stores the choice and hides the banner
  • Reject stores the minimal choice and hides the banner
  • Settings panel toggles categories; Save applies the selection
  • Essential category is always-on and disabled in the UI
  • Persisted to localStorage; not shown again on reload
  • Fade/slide-in animation

Concepts: localStorage · setTimeout · conditional rendering · controlled toggles
lessons.why:
• Store localStorage.consent = {accepted, categories}. On mount, read it; if present, render nothing.
  • Settings panel keeps local category booleans; Save writes to localStorage and closes.

lessons.name: Context Menu
lessons.desc: Right-click menus - positioning, viewport clamping, and dismissal.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Context Menu
lessons.what:
Build a ContextMenu component. Right-clicking a target opens a custom menu at the cursor with items (icons, disabled items, dividers). Left-click, ESC, or scrolling closes it. The menu must clamp to the viewport so it never overflows off-screen. Nested submenus are a bonus.

Requirements

  • Right-click (onContextMenu) opens the menu at the cursor position
  • Viewport-aware: menu position clamps so it never goes off-screen
  • Closes on outside left-click, ESC, scroll, and after an action
  • Items support disabled state, icons, and dividers
  • Nested submenus open to the right of their parent
  • Right-clicking an open menu item does not close the menu
  • First item focused on open

Concepts: onContextMenu · viewport clamping · window.innerWidth/Height · keyboard events
lessons.why:
• Measure the menu after render and clamp: left = min(x, innerWidth - rect.width - 8), top = min(y, innerHeight - rect.height - 8).
  • Dismissal: document mousedown listener checking the menu ref, plus scroll (capture: true) and contextmenu elsewhere.

lessons.name: Tic-Tac-Toe Game
lessons.desc: Google classic - state, win detection, and time travel.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Tic-Tac-Toe Game
lessons.what:
Build a TicTacToe game. Two players alternate X and O. Highlight the winning line, detect draws, and show a turn indicator plus a scoreboard. Add game history with undo and time travel (jump to any past move) and a restart button.

Requirements

  • Click an empty cell places the current player mark
  • Players alternate with a clear turn indicator
  • Win detection across all 8 lines; winning cells highlighted
  • Draw detection when the board is full with no winner
  • Scoreboard: X wins, O wins, draws
  • Restart button resets the board
  • History with undo and time travel to any move
  • No moves allowed after the game ends

Concepts: useState · winning combinations · derived state · immutable updates
lessons.why:
• Board = array(9). Winner check: predefined combos of 3 indices; find a combo where all three are equal and non-empty.
  • History = array of {board, player}. Time travel slices the history up to the target move index.

lessons.name: Calculator
lessons.desc: The classic vanilla JS machine coding - digit entry, decimal handling, and chained operations.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Calculator
lessons.what:
Build a Calculator with a display and buttons: digits, decimal point, +, -, x, /, %, +/-, Clear (C), and equals. Handle chained operations (5 + 3 = then + 2 =). Guard against divide-by-zero, leading decimals, multiple decimals per number, and leading zeros.

Requirements

  • All digits and the four basic operators work
  • Chained operations: 5 + 3 = 8, then + 2 = 10 (result becomes the left operand)
  • Decimal input: only one dot per number; "5." is valid
  • Divide by zero shows Error and requires a clear
  • +/- toggles the sign; % divides the current value by 100
  • Clear (C) resets everything; display shows the running value or expression
  • Keyboard support (digits, operators, Enter, Backspace) as a bonus

Concepts: state machine · operator precedence · string/number parsing · keyboard events
lessons.why:
• Track {display, left, operator, overwrite}. On a digit when overwrite is true, start a fresh number. On an operator, if left exists compute left = op(left, current).
  • Apply % and +/- to the current display value before pressing an operator or equals.

lessons.name: Color Swatch Picker
lessons.desc: Google color-appearing interview: RGB sliders, hex output, and a preview swatch.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Color Swatch Picker
lessons.what:
Build a ColorPicker with three sliders (R, G, B) each 0-255. A large swatch shows the current color. Display hex and rgb() values that update live. Support typing a validated hex value, a random-color button, and click-to-copy the hex.

Requirements

  • Three range sliders (R/G/B) update the color live
  • Swatch background reflects the current RGB
  • Hex and rgb() outputs update as the sliders move
  • Hex input validated (#RRGGBB); invalid input reverts
  • Random color button sets all three sliders
  • Click the hex to copy to clipboard (navigator.clipboard)
  • Number inputs beside sliders stay in sync

Concepts: controlled range inputs · toString(16) · two-way sync · clipboard
lessons.why:
• Single source of truth: {r,g,b}. Sliders and number inputs both write to it. Hex = "#" + [r,g,b].map(v => v.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("").
  • Hex input: match /^#?[0-9a-f]{6}$/i; on invalid, reset the input text to the current hex.

lessons.name: eCommerce Product Listing with Filters
lessons.desc: Flipkart UI2 round - categories, product cards, filters, and a wishlist.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? eCommerce Product Listing with Filters
lessons.what:
Build a ProductListing page. A sidebar with category, price-range, and rating filters; the main area renders product cards (image, title, price, rating, wishlist heart). Sort by price and rating. Show a result count and an empty state. Wishlist toggles persist to localStorage and update a header counter.

Requirements

  • Category filter (single-select)
  • Price range slider + minimum rating filter (combine via AND)
  • Sort dropdown: price asc/desc, rating desc
  • Result count reflects filters; empty state when nothing matches
  • Product cards: image, title, price with strikethrough MRP, rating badge, wishlist heart
  • Wishlist toggle updates a header counter and persists to localStorage
  • Filters apply instantly without a reload
  • Debounced price changes for smooth slider updates

Concepts: derived state · filter/sort pipelines · localStorage · debounce
lessons.why:
• Keep raw products[] plus filter state {category, maxPrice, minRating, sort}. Derive the visible list with useMemo, chaining filters then the sort.
  • Wishlist as a Set of ids in state, persisted on every change. Header count = set.size.

lessons.name: Weather App
lessons.desc: A full mini-app - city search, API fetching, unit toggle, and loading/error states.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Weather App
lessons.what:
Build a WeatherApp. Search by city (or use geolocation). Fetch from the Open-Meteo API or any mock. Show current temperature, condition, feels-like, and a 5-day forecast. Toggle Celsius/Fahrenheit. Persist the last city and unit, and handle loading, error, and empty states.

Requirements

  • City search input (debounced suggestions or Enter to search)
  • Current conditions: temp, condition, feels like, humidity, wind
  • 5-day forecast cards with icon and high/low
  • C / F unit toggle converts displayed values
  • Last city and unit persisted; reload auto-fetches
  • Loading spinner, error banner with retry, and an empty state
  • Uses a key-free API (e.g. Open-Meteo) or a mock

Concepts: useEffect + async · fetch · state machines · unit conversion
lessons.why:
• Model UI state as {status: idle|loading|error|success, data} separately from the data shape.
  • Convert f = c * 9/5 + 32 at render time; keep metric values as the source of truth.

lessons.name: Memory Match Game
lessons.desc: Classic grid game - flipped-card state, matching logic, and a moves timer.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Memory Match Game
lessons.what:
Build a MemoryGame. A grid of cards (4x4 default, configurable). Flip two cards; if they match they stay face-up, otherwise they flip back after 800ms. Track moves and time, detect the win, and restart by reshuffling.

Requirements

  • Grid of paired cards shuffled on start
  • Click flips a card; at most two face-up at a time
  • Match stays face-up; mismatch flips back after a delay
  • Input locked while two cards are resolving
  • Move counter and elapsed timer
  • Win detection plus a completion banner
  • Restart reshuffles and resets
  • Card count configurable (4x4, 6x6)

Concepts: useState · setTimeout · Fisher-Yates shuffle · game state machine
lessons.why:
• Cards = array of {id, value, matched}. Keep flippedIds (max 2). After the second flip, compare values and setTimeout 800ms to flip back on a mismatch.
  • Shuffle with Fisher-Yates: for i from n-1 down to 1, swap i with a random index in [0..i].

lessons.name: Poll / Vote Widget
lessons.desc: Vote, count, and results - a compact but complete data flow problem.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Poll / Vote Widget
lessons.what:
Build a Poll widget: a question and options with vote counts. Clicking an option highlights it as chosen, updates counts, and shows percentage result bars. Persist the vote in localStorage so the same user cannot vote again, and show live-updating totals.

Requirements

  • Render options with their vote counts
  • Clicking an option registers the vote and updates counts
  • Percentages shown on result bars after voting
  • Vote persisted to localStorage (one vote per user)
  • Results hidden until the first vote (configurable reveal mode)
  • Total vote count displayed
  • Voted option highlighted distinctly

Concepts: useState · percentage math · localStorage · immutable updates
lessons.why:
• State: {question, options: [{id, text, votes}], votedId}. On vote, map options to increment the chosen one and set votedId.
  • Percent = votes / total * 100. Result bar width = percent with a CSS transition on the fill.

lessons.name: Expense Tracker
lessons.desc: CRUD + totals + filtering - the essential dashboard-flavoured machine coding problem.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Expense Tracker
lessons.what:
Build an ExpenseTracker. Add expenses with description, amount, category, and date. List them with edit and delete. Show total spent, a per-category breakdown with progress bars, and a month filter. Persist everything to localStorage.

Requirements

  • Add expense form (description, amount, category, date)
  • Validation: description required, amount greater than 0
  • Expense list sorted newest first with edit + delete
  • Summary: total for the selected month and budget vs spent
  • Category breakdown with bars and per-category totals
  • Month filter (all months or a specific month)
  • Expenses persisted to localStorage
  • Edit mode fills the form; saving updates the entry

Concepts: useReducer · localStorage · filtering/summarising · form validation
lessons.why:
• State shape: [{id, desc, amount, category, date}]. Derive totals and breakdowns with useMemo from the filtered list.
  • For edit: an editingId state; the form initialises from that expense and dispatches UPDATE on save.

lessons.name: Markdown Preview Editor
lessons.desc: The classic editor-preview split - sanitise HTML and avoid re-rendering on every keystroke.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Markdown Preview Editor
lessons.what:
Build a MarkdownEditor. Left pane: a textarea. Right pane: live-rendered HTML. Support headings, bold/italic, links, inline code, code blocks, lists, and blockquotes. Sanitise the output (no raw script tags). Debounce the conversion and show character/word counts.

Requirements

  • Live preview updates as you type (debounced 200ms)
  • Support: # headings, **bold**, *italic*, [link](url), `code`, ```fences```, - lists, > quotes
  • Responsive two-column layout with editor-only / preview-only toggles
  • Sanitised HTML (strip script tags and onclick attributes)
  • Character and word counts in a status bar
  • Markdown persisted to localStorage

Concepts: controlled textarea · markdown parsing · sanitisation · debounce
lessons.why:
• Parse by line type (heading, blockquote, list) then inline-replace **text**, *text*, and `code` with regex.
  • Sanitise by escaping < to < in raw text first and emitting only your own safe tags - never pass user HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

lessons.name: Movie Seat Selector
lessons.desc: A booking UI with grid state - seat status, selection, and a live total.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Movie Seat Selector
lessons.what:
Build a SeatSelector. A screen label at the top and a grid of seats with states: available, taken, and selected. Click to toggle selection (taken seats are disabled). Show a legend, the selected count, a price total, and an order summary. Enforce a max selectable limit.

Requirements

  • Grid generated from rows x cols config
  • Three seat states: available / taken / selected
  • Taken seats (pre-seeded or from props) are not clickable
  • Selected count and running total update live
  • Max selectable limit (configurable, default 8)
  • Legend showing the seat colors
  • Screen label at the top
  • Checkout button enabled only when seats are selected

Concepts: 2D array state · Set for selection · derived totals · disable logic
lessons.why:
• Seats = 2D array of {id, status}. selected = Set of seat ids. Click toggles the id, skipping taken seats.
  • Total = selected.size * pricePerSeat. Show the summary only after the first selection.

lessons.name: Music Playlist UI (Atlassian)
lessons.desc: The Atlassian round: render a playlist, order, filter, and persist it.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Music Playlist UI (Atlassian)
lessons.what:
Build a Playlist component from track data [{id, title, artist, duration, plays}]. Render the list with a header, sort by title/artist/plays/duration, filter by search, show total duration, and support: play a track (highlight + show a mini player), remove a track, and reorder via up/down buttons or drag. Persist the playlist to localStorage.

Requirements

  • Render tracks with index, title, artist, duration, plays
  • Sort dropdown: title, artist, plays, duration (asc/desc)
  • Search box filters by title or artist
  • Total duration in the header updates with the filtered list
  • Click a track plays it (highlight + mini player shows it)
  • Remove a track and reorder via up/down or drag
  • Playlist persisted to localStorage
  • Empty state when no tracks match

Concepts: derived state · useMemo · sorting/filtering · localStorage
lessons.why:
• Derive the visible list from raw tracks + {sort, dir, query} with useMemo; keep raw data untouched.
  • Reorder: remove the item then insert at the target index - never mutate the array in place.

lessons.name: Virtual Scroll List from Scratch
lessons.desc: Render 100,000 rows without a library — the performance machine coding challenge.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Virtual Scroll List from Scratch
lessons.what:
Build a VirtualList component that renders only visible items from a large dataset. Support fixed and variable row heights. Smooth scroll. Scroll-to-index API.

Requirements

  • Only renders visible rows + small overscan buffer (3 rows above/below)
  • Fixed row height mode (most efficient)
  • Variable row height mode (measure with ResizeObserver or pre-measure)
  • scrollToIndex(idx) method exposed via ref
  • Show total item count, no DOM pollution
  • No flicker on fast scroll

Concepts: useRef · scroll events · CSS transform · ResizeObserver · useImperativeHandle
lessons.why:
• Container: fixed height, overflow-y:scroll. Inner: total height = rowCount * rowHeight (spacer). Only render rows in range [startIndex, endIndex].
  • startIndex = Math.floor(scrollTop / rowHeight). endIndex = Math.ceil((scrollTop + viewportHeight) / rowHeight). Offset visible rows with transform or top/paddingTop.

lessons.name: useForm Hook (Formik-lite)
lessons.desc: Build a reusable form management hook — abstraction design at its finest.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? useForm Hook (Formik-lite)
lessons.what:
Build a useForm(config) hook with: field registration, validation schema support, touched/dirty tracking, async submit handler, field-level and form-level errors, watch(field) for dependent fields.

Requirements

  • register(name, options): returns {value, onChange, onBlur, ref}
  • Validation: per-field validators run on blur and submit
  • touched: per-field boolean, set true on blur
  • dirty: true if value differs from initialValue
  • handleSubmit(fn): wraps fn, runs validation, calls fn only if valid
  • watch(field): re-render when field changes
  • setError/clearError API for server-side errors

Concepts: useRef · useReducer · closures · custom hooks · validation patterns
lessons.why:
• Store all state in a useRef (values, errors, touched, dirty). Only update state (via useState) when things that affect render change — avoids re-renders on every keystroke.
  • register: return a stable object using useMemo/useCallback. Stable refs prevent child re-renders when using with React.memo.

lessons.name: Build useQuery (mini React Query)
lessons.desc: The hardest custom hook challenge — caching, deduplication, stale-while-revalidate.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Build useQuery (mini React Query)
lessons.what:
Build useQuery(key, fetchFn, options) hook with: automatic fetching, stale-while-revalidate caching, background refetch on window focus, deduplication (same key in-flight only fetches once), and manual refetch.

Requirements

  • Returns {data, error, isLoading, isFetching, refetch}
  • Cache results by key (use a module-level Map)
  • Show stale data while refetching in background (isFetching=true but data visible)
  • Deduplicate: same key requested by two components = one network call
  • refetch on window focus (configurable: refetchOnWindowFocus option)
  • staleTime option: treat cached data as fresh for N ms

Concepts: useEffect · useRef · module-level cache · subscriptions · window events
lessons.why:
• Module-level cache Map: key → {data, timestamp, promise}. On fetch: check if key is in-flight (existing promise), if yes share that promise.
  • For stale-while-revalidate: return cached data immediately (isLoading=false, isFetching=true), fetch in background, update cache and re-render on resolve.

lessons.name: Build a Mini React Router
lessons.desc: Understand browser history, context, and nested routing by building it yourself.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Build a Mini React Router
lessons.what:
Build BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link, useParams, and useNavigate. Support nested routes, dynamic segments (:id), and programmatic navigation.

Requirements

  • BrowserRouter: listen to popstate, provide router context
  • Routes: find the best matching Route and render it
  • Route: match path (support :param segments)
  • Link: renders , calls navigate on click, no full reload
  • useParams: return current route params from URL
  • useNavigate: return navigate(path) function that pushes to history
  • Nested routes: child Routes resolve relative to parent

Concepts: Context · history API · pattern matching · useEffect · useRef
lessons.why:
• Router context: {location, navigate}. Listen to popstate event to update location. navigate = (path) => { history.pushState({}, "", path); dispatchEvent(new PopStateEvent("popstate")); }.
  • Route matching: convert path "/users/:id" to regex. Extract param names. On match, store params in context for useParams.

lessons.name: Resizable Split Panels
lessons.desc: Mouse event math + constraints + performance — a real UI engineering challenge.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Resizable Split Panels
lessons.what:
Build a SplitPanel component that renders two panels with a draggable divider. Support horizontal and vertical splits, min/max size constraints, persist split position, and collapse either panel.

Requirements

  • Drag divider resizes panels in real time
  • Minimum size constraint per panel (minSize prop)
  • Maximum size constraint (maxSize prop)
  • Horizontal and vertical split modes
  • Double-click divider to collapse/expand a panel
  • Persist panel sizes to localStorage
  • Smooth — no lag on fast mouse movement

Concepts: useRef · mouse events · pointer events · CSS · useCallback
lessons.why:
• On mousedown on divider: attach mousemove and mouseup to document (not the divider). On mousemove: calculate delta from start position. Clamp new sizes within min/max.
  • Use pointer events instead of mouse events for touch support. setPointerCapture on the divider on pointerdown.

lessons.name: Build a Mini State Management Library
lessons.desc: Build Zustand from scratch — the ultimate React architecture challenge.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Build a Mini State Management Library
lessons.what:
Build createStore(initialState) returning a hook useStore(selector). Support: atomic subscriptions (only re-render when selected slice changes), actions (store.setState), middleware, and a devtools-like getSnapshot.

Requirements

  • createStore(initialState) returns a useStore hook
  • useStore(selector): component re-renders only when selector(state) changes
  • setState(partial | updater): merges partial state or calls updater(prev)
  • Subscriptions: internal pub-sub, listeners per component
  • Middleware support: intercept setState calls
  • getState() and subscribe(listener) on the store object

Concepts: useRef · useSyncExternalStore · pub-sub · shallow equality · closures
lessons.why:
• Use React 18's useSyncExternalStore(store.subscribe, () => selector(store.getState())). It handles concurrent mode correctly.
  • Shallow equality check in the selector: only call forceUpdate if shallowEqual(prevSelected, nextSelected) returns false.

lessons.name: Undo / Redo with Command Pattern
lessons.desc: History management — used in collaborative editors, canvas apps, and form UIs.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Undo / Redo with Command Pattern
lessons.what:
Build a reusable useHistory hook implementing undo/redo. Apply it to a simple drawing canvas or text editor. Each action is a Command with execute() and undo() methods.

Requirements

  • useHistory returns { state, execute(command), undo, redo, canUndo, canRedo }
  • Command interface: { execute, undo, description }
  • undo() reverts the last command
  • redo() reapplies a reverted command
  • Redo stack clears when new command is executed
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+Z (undo), Ctrl+Y/Ctrl+Shift+Z (redo)
  • Max history size (configurable, default 50)

Concepts: useReducer · command pattern · keyboard events · immutability
lessons.why:
• State: { past: [commands], future: [commands] }. execute: append to past, clear future. undo: pop from past, push to future, call command.undo(). redo: pop from future, push to past, call command.execute().
  • Apply commands to a separate "working state" ref. Past/future store commands only (not snapshots) — this scales to large state.

lessons.name: File Explorer (Tree View)
lessons.desc: Atlassian P40 and MakeMyTrip both asked this - nested tree with lazy loading.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? File Explorer (Tree View)
lessons.what:
Build a FileExplorer. Render a nested folder/file tree. Click a folder to expand or collapse. Folders load children lazily (async on first expand) with loading and error states. Support icons, selection, keyboard navigation (arrows, Enter), and a breadcrumb of the selected path.

Requirements

  • Recursive tree rendering of folders and files
  • Expand/collapse folders with a chevron indicator
  • Lazy loading: children fetched on first expand (mock API with delay)
  • Loading spinner and retry on fetch failure
  • Select a file or folder; highlight it; show its path in a breadcrumb
  • Keyboard: Up/Down move selection, Right expands, Left collapses, Enter opens
  • Side panel shows selected file size and type metadata

Concepts: recursive components · async state · useCallback · keyboard events · tree data structures
lessons.why:
• Normalise the tree into Map for O(1) selection and expansion. Expand state = Set of expanded ids.
