  • Lazy load: node.children === undefined and node.isFolder -> show a spinner, fetch, then set children. Cache results so re-expanding never refetches.

lessons.name: Nested Comments (Reddit-style)
lessons.desc: Atlassian and MakeMyTrip favourite - recursive rendering with immutable updates.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Nested Comments (Reddit-style)
lessons.what:
Build a CommentSection with unlimited nesting. Per comment: reply, edit, delete (removing descendants), and like. Replies render recursively under their parent. Add a top-level input plus an inline reply box per comment. Every update must be immutable - never mutate the tree.

Requirements

  • Comment tree rendered recursively to unlimited depth
  • Reply opens an inline input under that comment
  • Edit swaps the comment text with an inline textarea
  • Delete removes the comment and its descendants (with confirm)
  • Like/dislike counter toggle
  • Collapse/expand hides and shows a comment children
  • Top-level comment input
  • Persisted to localStorage
  • Sort: newest first or most voted (toggle)

Concepts: recursion · immutable tree updates · useReducer · reconciliation
lessons.why:
• Comment node: {id, author, text, votes, children, createdAt}. For updates, walk the tree and rebuild each level, replacing only the matching id - fresh references everywhere.
  • Helper: updateTree(comments, id, fn) returns a new array where the matched node is replaced by fn(node) and every ancestor is rebuilt.

lessons.name: Chat App UI
lessons.desc: Flipkart WhatsApp-clone round - message list, input, and simulated auto-replies.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Chat App UI
lessons.what:
Build a ChatApp: a contact list on the left and a conversation pane with messages (left = received, right = sent), a header, and a message input. Enter sends the message and after a delay the other user auto-replies from a canned list. Show timestamps, bubbles with tails, a typing indicator, read ticks, and unread badges.

Requirements

  • Message list auto-scrolls to the bottom on a new message
  • Bubbles: sent right (blue), received left (grey), with timestamps
  • Typing indicator while the simulated reply is pending
  • Auto-reply from canned responses after 1-2s
  • Left pane: contacts with last message preview and unread badge
  • Read receipt: double ticks turn blue when read
  • Enter to send; input disabled while empty
  • Chat persisted to localStorage

Concepts: useRef for auto-scroll · useEffect · timers · derived previews
lessons.why:
• Auto-scroll: scrollRef.current.scrollIntoView() in a useEffect keyed on messages.length - but only when the user is near the bottom.
  • Typing indicator: a pendingReply state; show a typing bubble while true, then resolve it into the reply message.

lessons.name: Minesweeper
lessons.desc: Google classic - board generation, flood-fill reveal, and win/loss detection.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Minesweeper
lessons.what:
Build a Minesweeper game. Generate an N x M board with a configurable mine count. Left-click reveals a cell; a mine ends the game. Revealing a 0-adjacent cell flood-fills the empty region. Right-click flags. Show a remaining-mine counter and timer. Win when every safe cell is revealed. Difficulty presets: Beginner 9x9/10, Intermediate 16x16/40, Expert 30x16/99.

Requirements

  • Board generation with configurable size and mine count
  • First click is never a mine (defer placement or regenerate)
  • Adjacent-mine numbers shown on reveal
  • Flood-fill reveal for 0-adjacent cells (BFS/DFS)
  • Right-click flags; flags counted against remaining mines
  • Timer starts on the first reveal
  • Win: all safe cells revealed. Loss: reveal all mines on a mine click
  • Restart and difficulty presets

Concepts: 2D arrays · flood fill (BFS/DFS) · randomness · game state machine
lessons.why:
• Cells = 2D array of {mine, revealed, flagged, adj}. Place mines, then compute adj for each cell by scanning its 8 neighbours.
  • Flood fill: when a 0-adjacent cell is revealed, BFS its unrevealed neighbours and reveal them, stopping at numbered cells.

lessons.name: Snake Game
lessons.desc: The classic arcade game on a grid - game loop, collision, and score.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Snake Game
lessons.what:
Build a Snake game on a grid. Arrow keys (or WASD) change direction; the snake moves on a fixed interval that speeds up as it eats food. Eating grows the snake and increments the score. Hitting a wall or yourself ends the game with an overlay and restart. Show score and high score (localStorage).

Requirements

  • Snake moves continuously on a grid (interval-based game loop)
  • Arrow/WASD controls with direction lock (no reversing into itself)
  • Food spawns at a random free cell; eating grows the snake
  • Speed increases with score (interval shortens)
  • Wall or self collision = game over with overlay
  • Score and high score (persisted) displayed
  • Pause/resume (Space) and restart
  • Rendered as divs or canvas

Concepts: game loop · queue (snake body) · collision detection · useRef for state
lessons.why:
• Snake = array of {x,y} cells, head first. Move: unshift the new head, pop the tail unless eating. Keep snake/direction in refs so the interval closure reads fresh values.
  • Direction lock: reject a turn when (dx + nx) === 0 and (dy + ny) === 0.

lessons.name: Calendar / Date Range Picker
lessons.desc: Booking and analytics dashboards everywhere - month grids, range logic, and keyboard nav.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Calendar / Date Range Picker
lessons.what:
Build a DateRangePicker: a month grid with prev/next navigation. The first click sets the range start, the second completes it (in-range dates highlighted). Clicking when a range exists starts a new one. Support presets, min/max constraints, keyboard navigation, and onChange({start, end}).

Requirements

  • Month grid: weekday headers, correct day alignment, today highlighted
  • Prev/Next month navigation plus a jump-to-today
  • Range selection: first click start, second end; hover previews in-range
  • Clicking when a range exists starts a new range
  • Presets: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, This month, Last 30 days
  • Dates outside min/max disabled
  • Keyboard: arrows move focus, Enter selects, Escape cancels
  • onChange({start, end}) with start <= end

Concepts: Date object · date arithmetic · range logic · grid generation
lessons.why:
• Grid: firstDay = new Date(y, m, 1), offset = firstDay.getDay(), then fill 42 cells (6 weeks).
  • Range logic: if start && !end && date >= start -> set end. Otherwise set start = date, end = null. If end < start, restart the range.

lessons.name: Login / Profile Flow with Protected Routes
lessons.desc: Flipkart asks the full flow - login, session, protected routing, and profile.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Login / Profile Flow with Protected Routes
lessons.what:
Build an AuthFlow demo: a login form with mock validation, a session Context, and protected routes. Unauthenticated users redirect to /login (then return to the requested page). A profile page shows the user with logout. Simulate a fake API with delays and error paths, and persist the session token in localStorage.

Requirements

  • Login form: email + password with validation and error messages
  • Fake auth API (Promise with delay) with success and failure paths
  • Session in Context + persisted to localStorage
  • ProtectedRoute redirects unauthenticated users to /login
  • After login, redirect back to the originally requested route
  • Profile page shows user info; logout clears the session
  • Signup tab validates password confirmation
  • Loading state on the submit button

Concepts: Context · protected routing · localStorage · redirect logic · form validation
lessons.why:
• Session Context: {user, token, login, logout, loading}. On mount, read localStorage.token and validate it (mock).
  • ProtectedRoute: if loading show a spinner; if no user return . Login reads state.from to redirect back.

lessons.name: Error Boundary
lessons.desc: Resilience in React - class boundaries and the modern async-error hook.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Error Boundary
lessons.what:
Build an ErrorBoundary class component with fallback UI, reset, and error reporting. Handle render errors and, via a useErrorHandler hook, async errors thrown in effects or callbacks.

Requirements

  • Class component using getDerivedStateFromError and componentDidCatch
  • Renders fallback UI (children or default) instead of crashing the app
  • Reset button clears the error and retries rendering children
  • Reports error + errorInfo to an onError callback
  • useErrorHandler(err) throws inside a callback so async errors reach the boundary
  • Multiple boundaries wrap different regions of the app
  • Boundary keyed so state resets cleanly

Concepts: class components · getDerivedStateFromError · componentDidCatch · error reporting
lessons.why:
• class ErrorBoundary extends Component { static getDerivedStateFromError(error) { return {error}; } componentDidCatch(error, info) { onError?.(error, info); } }
  • useErrorHandler keeps a ref to setState and returns (err) => { if (err) throwRef.current(err); } - throwing inside the boundary subtree triggers it.

lessons.name: Custom Hooks Library
lessons.desc: Every senior React round - a toolbox of production hooks with stable references.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Custom Hooks Library
lessons.what:
Build a library of reusable hooks: useDebouncedValue, useLocalStorage, useClickOutside, useWindowSize, usePrevious, and useIntersection. Each must clean up after itself, return stable references, and be generic. Write a small demo page exercising every hook.

Requirements

  • useDebouncedValue(value, delay): returns the value after delay of no changes
  • useLocalStorage(key, initial): reads on mount, writes on change, syncs across tabs
  • useClickOutside(ref, handler): mousedown outside triggers the handler, removes listener on unmount
  • useWindowSize(): returns {width, height}, updates debounced
  • usePrevious(value): returns the previous render value
  • useIntersection(ref, options): returns {isIntersecting, entry} via IntersectionObserver
  • All return stable references (no new functions every render)

Concepts: custom hooks · useCallback/useMemo · useEffect cleanup · generics
lessons.why:
• useDebouncedValue: useEffect with a setTimeout(delay) that sets state; clearTimeout in cleanup so each value change restarts the timer.
  • useLocalStorage: useState initialised from the key, useEffect writing on change, plus a window "storage" listener to sync other tabs.
